summary: WS binary-frame reorder behind corporate proxy leaves unclosed JSON chunk and partial tokens in multiplexed stream
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that long-running WebSocket chat streams periodically end with an unclosed JSON choice and duplicated partial tokens when the client is behind a corporate proxy/fanout. Impact:
- End users receive an incomplete JSON object and client SDK parse errors; conversations stop rendering and must be retried.
- Symptoms appear for ~8% of long streams (>30s) from the BrightDocs dedicated deployment.
Environment:
- BrightDocs dedicated account on prod us-east-1, API gateway + our edge proxy cluster in same region. Runs redwood-rlhf-7b model pinned at v2026-02-15. Customer using JS SDK v2.4.1 over browser WebSocket with multiplexed session mode.
Steps to reproduce (observed by customer):
1) Start a multiplexed WS session with two concurrent chat streams from a browser behind the corporate proxy; keep one stream open > 30s with streaming responses.
2) After intermittent network activity (edge probe or proxy rebind), the client receives what appears to be a fragmented binary frame sequence.
3) Client logs show partial JSON payloads (no closing brace) and duplicated token prefixes when reconnect/resume occurs.
4) The SDK fails to reassemble the final choice and throws a parse exception; UI shows partial sentence and stops.
Observed logs / errors from customer:
- "SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input" in SDK parser on final message.
- Client debug shows WS frames arriving with non-monotonic frame indices and duplicate prefix bytes.
- TCP-level traces show the corporate proxy coalescing and reordering SSE/WS fragments during a keepalive probe.
Additional notes:
- Customer reports workaround: switching to plain (non-multiplexed) single-session WS eliminated the failure in their tests.
- Problem occurs less frequently from non-corporate networks (home/other cloud), suggesting middlebox involvement.
comments: Support (Aisha): Triage - Received from BrightDocs support rep on 2026-03-10 14:20. Reproduced once in staging using a local proxy shim that injects reorder/fragment behavior.
CS (Jordan Lin): Confirmed customer is on dedicated plan and provided request IDs for several failed streams: rq_20260310_87fd, rq_20260310_94ab. Asking SRE for edge proxy request logs.

SRE (Mateo): Pulling edge-proxy logs and TCP captures for the time windows. Initial look shows several FIN/ACK + keepalive sequences coalesced by the upstream corporate proxy leading to out-of-order WS fragments at our gateway.
Action: capture 1h of pcap for customer IP and correlate with request IDs.

Eng (Priya): Hypothesis - our WS multiplexing expects ordered binary frame delivery for chunk assembly; if upstream shuffles small TCP segments we can observe partial JSON reassembly failure. Suggest adding defensive reordering detection and buffer until a complete JSON message boundary is observed. Will spike patch to SDK and server-side parser.

Customer (BrightDocs): Confirmed we can reproduce reliably when using corporate proxy appliance A with aggressive connection pooling. Non-corporate networks do not reproduce. We can provide packet captures on request.
Support (Aisha): Requested packet captures and browser network logs. Provided runbook checklist for collecting pcap + HAR and steps to toggle to single-session mode as temporary mitigation.
investigation_notes: Reproduced in internal staging by running a simple TCP proxy that reorders and coalesces segments: final JSON chunk occasionally missing closing brace when server's stream boundary arrives split across reordered frames.

Edge-proxy (v1.12.0) is seen forwarding WS binary frames with no additional per-message-sequence metadata; server assumes reliable in-order delivery from TCP but does not validate message-level completeness before handing to SDK assembler.

Client SDK (js v2.4.1) assembles frames eagerly into JSON and triggers parse when it sees what it believes to be end-of-message; if the end marker is delayed due to reordered frames, incomplete parse error occurs and resume logic can re-send previous prefix leading to duplicate tokens.

Sporadic correlation with our keepalive/probe timings on the edge: when upstream closes and reopens connection quickly, fragments can be replayed or delivered out of sequence to the gateway thread handling multiplexed sessions.
No evidence of model-side truncation or runtime OOM; logs show server emitted complete chunks but gateway delivered partial sequences to client on occasion.
Related internal ticket INT-420 tracked a separate proxy half-close case last quarter; concepts overlap but root here is binary-frame reorder at the corporate middlebox.

Proof-of-concept server-side mitigation: buffer binary frame bytes for a short, configurable reorder window (25ms) and validate JSON boundary before emitting to SDK assembly layer. Initial tests reduce failure rate from ~8% to <0.5% in synthetic workloads.
Client-side mitigation: SDK change to be lenient on parse errors for end-of-stream, attempt to re-request suffix or hold parse until next fragment arrives, and dedupe prefix on resume.
logs_and_traces: Edge proxy request IDs: rq_20260310_87fd, rq_20260310_94ab
action_items: SRE: retrieve and attach full pcap for both failed request IDs and keep for postmortem (owner: Mateo, due 2026-03-11)
Eng: implement short reorder-buffer on gateway and add JSON-boundary validation in assembler (owner: Priya, spike by 2026-03-13)
SDK: implement parse-retry and prefix-deduplication on resume in js SDK (owner: Lillian, target 2.4.2 release)
Support: advise customer to use single-session WS mode as interim mitigation and collect HAR + pcap (owner: Aisha)
CS: schedule coordinated snapshot with customer to reproduce while we capture pcap (owner: Jordan, scheduled 2026-03-11 09:00 UTC)
Postmortem: prepare incident writeup if regression persists after fixes (owner: Mateo)
Follow-up: add a conformance test that simulates reordered TCP segments for streaming to prevent regressions (owner: Eng QA)
Communications: send interim status to BrightDocs and note workaround and ETA (owner: Aisha)
Related PR: runtime change referenced for tracking: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2891
resolution: Work in progress - mitigation patch merged to internal branch and SDK change under review. Customer using single-session WS as temporary workaround. Close after production rollouts and customer validation.
resolution_notes: 03/12: Gateway reorder-buffer spike showed <0.5% failure in staging; pushed internal canary to 5% of edge traffic for further validation.
03/12: BrightDocs validated single-session WS workaround; confirmed failure rate drops to near zero in their environment.
Next: Roll gateway fix to prod edge pool after QA; publish SDK 2.4.2 containing parse-retry and dedupe logic, and coordinate with BrightDocs to remove workaround.
If customer still observed issues after rollouts, escalate to network team for joint debug with their proxy vendor (customer requested vendor involvement if problem persists).
